“Impulse approximation’’ means that the external probe (electromagnetic, weak, …) sees the nucleus as a collection of independent, free-like nucleons and interacts with only one of them, while the rest act merely as spectators.  For this picture to hold we must assume

• the current couples to a single nucleon (so no two–body exchange currents are included) → assumption 1;  
• the other nucleons do not distort either the incoming probe or the struck nucleon’s outgoing wave, i.e. the nucleus is effectively transparent → assumption 2;  
• the struck nucleon is taken to behave as if it were free, i.e. its nuclear binding can be ignored during the short interaction time → assumption 4.  

Whether the quarks inside that nucleon are relativistic or not (assumption 3) is irrelevant to the impulse approximation; the picture works equally well in relativistic formulations.

Hence the three necessary and sufficient assumptions are 1, 2 and 4.

Answer: C
